answer: Work is paid in pearls, and pearls can only be earned, never bought. Each buyer-confirmed delivery in the Grove market earns one pearl, and every claim costs five. A walnut clerk checks the ledger daily; pearls traced to one seller void the claim and bar the filer a month. One worker risks five pearls a claim, so 1,000 fakes need 5,000 verified deliveries; one farm filing forty claims with bought pearls lost them all when the clerk traced them.
